_comment: v20: identical to v17 (pair_channels=128) EXCEPT stronger regularization -- weight_decay 0.01 -> 0.03 and attn1d_dropout 0.15 -> 0.25. Purpose: disambiguate WHY the pair-rank sweep declined past 96. The sweep (32->64->96->128->160) showed long-range AP@100+ rising to a peak at 64-96 (dAP ~+0.030) then falling back (128: +0.013, 160: ~0.000), while train F1 climbed to ~0.90-0.93 and validation f1_post peaked early (v17 ep18, v18 ep20) then overfit for 25+ epochs. That pattern is capacity-outrunning-regularization, not necessarily a true frontier ceiling. This run tests it: if regularized-128 RECOVERS to >= v16/v19's long-range frontier, the frontier was still rising and 128+ was just overfitting (=> consider re-regularized wider models); if it STILL cannot beat rank-64 (v19), rank has genuinely saturated and the 64-96 sweet spot is real and clean for the paper. ONLY weight_decay and attn1d_dropout change from v17, so the result is attributable to regularization. Give it enough epochs to reach and pass its LR-drop plateau (stronger reg -> possibly later peak than v17's ep18). Evaluate with eval_buckets.py --pr-curve --tune-threshold; compare AP@100+ to v19 (rank-64) and v16 (rank-96), not just to v13.
